calibration: 5 is a typical idea pitched at an SF startup event.
7 is an idea a good seed fund would take a meeting on.
9 is rare: top few percent of funded seed-stage ideas.
10 is reserved for overwhelming evidence. Expect almost none.
Use the whole range. Two mediocre ideas can both get 4.

criteria.name: Problem severity and urgency
criteria.question: How badly does a specific group need this solved, right now?
lookFor: signs of active searching or spending

anchors.text: Vitamin. No identifiable sufferer, or a mild inconvenience nobody acts on.
Real but occasional or low stakes. People shrug and live with it.
Recurring pain for a definable group. Some use clunky workarounds.
Hair on fire for a specific persona. Budget exists, people search for fixes, workarounds are expensive.
Existential or mandated: lost revenue, compliance deadlines, safety. Buyers would take a half-working product today.

criteria.name: Market size and growth
criteria.question: How big is the market this can reach within five years, sized bottom-up, and is it growing?
lookFor: a believable serviceable market, not just TAM
for local ideas, a credible expansion path

anchors.text: Reachable market under about $50M, or impossible to size.
Niche, $50M to $500M, flat.
$500M to $2B, or smaller but growing above 25% a year.
$2B to $10B with healthy growth and a credible bottom-up build.
Above $10B, bottom-up math checks out, growing.

caps.when: Sizing is top-down only ("1% of a $50B market")
Market numbers have no evidence ID and the reasoning is loose

criteria.name: Willingness to pay and business model
criteria.question: Who pays, how much, and do the unit economics plausibly work?

anchors.text: Nobody obvious pays, or "ads later".
A payer exists but is price sensitive. Margins unclear.
Clear payer with a pricing analog. Plausible margins.
Payer has budget and precedent prices. Gross margin above 60% is plausible. LTV over CAC holds up.
Customers already pay similar prices for worse alternatives. Strong margins. Expansion revenue built in.

caps.when: The payer is not the user and there is no plan to reach the payer

criteria.name: Differentiation vs alternatives
criteria.question: Compared with what customers do today, including doing nothing, is this clearly better?
lookFor: spreadsheets, interns, agencies and doing nothing
the one dimension where it is much better

anchors.text: Me-too in a crowded space.
Cheaper or nicer than strong incumbents. Incremental.
Meaningfully better on one dimension customers care about.
10x better on a dimension that matters, for a segment incumbents serve badly.
New category or no credible alternative, and the status quo is painful.

criteria.name: Defensibility
criteria.question: If this works, what stops a well-funded copycat in year three?

anchors.text: Nothing. Anyone can clone it in a weekend.
Head start only.
One plausible moat that builds over time.
A compounding moat (data or network effects) with a clear path to it.
Several reinforcing moats. Incumbents structurally can't follow.

caps.when: A thin wrapper on someone else's model with no data or workflow lock-in
Lives inside one platform (app store, API, marketplace) with no mitigation

criteria.name: Why now
criteria.question: What changed recently that makes this possible or necessary, and why didn't it work five years ago?
lookFor: signs the market is moving now

anchors.text: No reason it couldn't have been built in 2010. Or too early: depends on things that don't exist yet.
A vague trend ("AI is big").
A real enabling change, but one everyone has access to.
A specific recent change (cost curve, regulation, behavior shift) with a visible window.
A sharp, datable shift opens a window that will close, and the market is already moving.

criteria.name: Go-to-market
criteria.question: How do the first 10 customers, then the first 1,000, find and buy this?

anchors.text: "It'll go viral." Build it and they will come.
A channel is named but expensive or unproven. Long sales cycle with no entry point.
A plausible channel and a specific first segment.
Named first customers or communities, a cheap channel, a short sales cycle.
Built-in distribution (virality, marketplace liquidity, existing channel access) with evidence.

criteria.name: Feasibility and execution risk
criteria.question: Can a small team ship a useful v1 in about six months, and what could kill it?

anchors.text: Needs a scientific breakthrough, illegal activity, or billions in capex.
Major technical or regulatory risk with no plan.
Buildable. Real but manageable risks.
Clear build path. Risks named with mitigations.
v1 ships in weeks with off-the-shelf parts. Low regulatory exposure.

caps.when: A regulatory showstopper with no plan

criteria.name: Venture scale
criteria.question: Beyond the first market, can this become a $1B+ company?

anchors.text: Lifestyle business ceiling.
Could reach $10M ARR. Hard to see past it.
A path to $100M ARR through expansion.
A credible $1B outcome with several expansion paths.
Platform potential. Could define a $10B+ category.
